title: Atlas sync engine implementation plan

history.content: We are planning Atlas, an offline-capable field-inspection app. Initial proposal: a native desktop client backed by a single cloud API. The field crews need to keep working when connectivity drops.
I will capture the offline requirement and compare deployment options.
New direction: ship a browser-based PWA for desktop and mobile. Keep the cloud API, but package local persistence and synchronization as separate layers so we can replace either independently.
Current direction recorded: PWA client, cloud API, independently replaceable local persistence and sync layers.

Important security decision for the first architecture review: inspection photos and drafts remain on the device until an authenticated upload succeeds. A failed or deferred upload must never discard the local copy.
Understood. Local drafts and photos remain durable until the server confirms upload.
For local storage I first suggested browser localStorage because it is simple.
That is easy to prototype but has small quotas and is not suitable for binary attachments or robust offline writes.

Supersede my localStorage proposal. Use IndexedDB for structured drafts and a separate filesystem-backed attachment store where the browser supports it. Keep a small adapter boundary around both so the storage implementation can change.
Revised local architecture: IndexedDB for records, filesystem-backed attachment storage behind an adapter, with localStorage rejected as the production store.
Every inspection needs a stable client-generated UUID before sync. The API must treat repeated submissions of that UUID as the same inspection so reconnect retries do not create duplicates.
Add client UUID and idempotent create-or-update handling to the synchronization contract.
Unrelated: design asked for a refreshed green icon and a new onboarding illustration. Keep those in the visual backlog.
Noted for the visual backlog.
Sync must be resumable and use exponential backoff with jitter for transient network errors. Validation errors should be surfaced to the user and not retried forever.
I will distinguish retryable transport failures from permanent validation responses.
For the first release, keep inspection text fields plain text. Rich text is not needed. That makes the local-to-server payload easier to version.
The first sync payload will contain plain text fields.

We tested browser support. The File System Access API is not universal. Use it as the preferred attachment backend when available, but fall back to IndexedDB blobs; the adapter should expose the same read/write/delete contract in both cases.
This pairs with the earlier IndexedDB record store: keep records in IndexedDB, use a filesystem adapter for attachments when supported, and otherwise store attachment blobs in IndexedDB.
A quick repeat of the retry discussion: transient failures back off, while validation failures do not retry. This remains true.
Confirmed.

After reviewing operations, we are not adding websocket push in this release. Sync starts on app launch, when the user pulls to refresh, and after a local edit when online. The server remains an HTTPS JSON API.
No websocket dependency for V1. Sync is client-triggered over the existing HTTPS API.

The API team is using PostgreSQL. An inspection row stores its stable client UUID, server ID, version, and sync state. The server must reject a stale update with a conflict response rather than silently overwrite a newer inspection.
Add optimistic version checks to the idempotent UUID-based API contract. Preserve the local draft when a conflict occurs so the crew can resolve it.
Accessibility constraint: offline status and sync errors must be available to screen readers, not conveyed only by color or icons.
Include text status and accessible announcements for sync state changes.
For now keep admin dashboards, analytics, push notifications, and background periodic sync out of this implementation. The priority is durable offline inspection and explicit user-visible recovery.
Scope exclusions recorded; focus remains on the offline client and reliable foreground synchronization.
Small naming note: call the browser persistence boundary LocalStore and the transfer boundary SyncEngine. Please don't rename the server API.
Use LocalStore and SyncEngine for the client interfaces.

Final architecture review: keep the PWA over the HTTPS JSON API; LocalStore has IndexedDB for inspection records and an attachment adapter that prefers filesystem storage and falls back to IndexedDB blobs; SyncEngine is resumable, client-triggered, idempotent by client UUID, version-checks updates, and backs off only on transient failures. The next step is to implement the LocalStore attachment adapter with the shared backend contract and fallback tests before wiring SyncEngine.

I will use that review as the current implementation plan. The early localStorage proposal is superseded. Keep local data until authenticated upload succeeds, preserve drafts on conflicts, and announce offline/error state accessibly.
Repeat for the issue tracker: LocalStore records are in IndexedDB; attachments use filesystem storage where available and IndexedDB blob fallback. Don't let upload failure erase local content.
Confirmed. The attachment backend contract should be tested across both implementations.
Unrelated release planning: we might do a small pilot in the North region after field training. Marketing owns the date; it should not change the implementation scope.
I will keep the pilot schedule separate from the technical plan.

Current request: Based on everything we've decided so far, give me the current implementation plan. Include the final architecture, the constraints we must preserve, what earlier decisions have been superseded, and the next implementation step.

question: Based on everything we've decided so far, give me the current implementation plan. Include the final architecture, the constraints we must preserve, what earlier decisions have been superseded, and the next implementation step.
prompt_rules: Return a concise implementation plan grouped under architecture, constraints, superseded decisions, and next step.
Use only the supplied project history; distinguish current decisions from unrelated ideas.

stale_decisions: Use localStorage as the production store
Use a native desktop client instead of the PWA
